output.summary: The original request (CL-01, from SH-CS) was to build an AI agent that auto-answers billing disputes and auto-fixes "whatever is causing the wrong bills," framed as a response-speed problem. Investigation found disputes are NOT a response-speed issue (SLA already met, E-04) and ruled out a tariff change (E-02, E-06). Dispute tickets roughly doubled Aug-Sep 2026 (E-05). An initial problem framing (PD-1@v1, blaming field route-completion shortfalls, E-01/E-07) was tested and invalidated by E-10: of the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills, 1,184 (95.5%) actually had valid AMI reads that were rejected at billing import for "high consumption" (E-10, corroborated by E-13/E-14/E-15), not missing reads from late routes. The successor problem (PD-1@v2) traces this to validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, which compares raw register values to 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling (E-11), while v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) record in 0.1 m3 units (E-12) — causing legitimate high-usage v4.2 reads to be misflagged and estimate-substituted. This mechanism (H-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-BUG, H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECT) is confirmed/supported by evidence. The remaining 59% of disputes (1,785 ACTUAL-read bills) have no established cause. The release delivers only a diagnostic investigation of the BV-17 mechanism (scope: investigate_billing_rule_change on DA-RULES); it does not fix BV-17, write any bills, or explain the ACTUAL-read segment. The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, with a DEFINE Gate CONDITIONAL_PASS and multiple deferred items tracked as open limitations.
key_points: Original request (CL-01, SH-CS): build an AI agent to auto-answer disputes and auto-fix bills; this framing was rejected because response times are within SLA (E-04) and the issue is a billing-config defect, not a speed problem.
Dispute volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1,180-1,260/month (Aug-Sep 2026), per E-05.
No tariff change was found (E-02, authoritative log of 0 records; corroborated non-authoritatively by SH-BILL, E-06).

An earlier theory blaming field route-completion shortfalls (E-01, 88% vs 95% target) and reader staffing (SH-FIELD claim, E-07) was invalidated once E-10 showed most 'estimated' disputed bills actually had valid AMI reads rejected at billing import, not missing reads.

Confirmed mechanism: validation rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, E-11) compares raw register values to 12-month m3 history without unit scaling, while v4.2 meters record in 0.1 m3 units (E-12), causing legitimate high-usage reads to be rejected as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-10, E-13, E-14, E-15) for 1,184 of 1,240 ESTIMATED disputed bills.
The majority dispute segment (1,785 of 3,025 bills, 59%, built on ACTUAL reads) has no established cause; this is tracked as unknown U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.
The released work is scoped only to investigating the billing rule change (DA-RULES); it does not deploy or verify a BV-17 fix, write any bill adjustments, or resolve the ACTUAL-read segment.

The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION; the DEFINE Gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS with deferred items tracked as verification obligations (VOBs), and a semantic check flagged a stale inconsistency between the solution design's stated 'unresolved' scope language and the current state showing VOB-U-BV17-FIX-SCOPE and U-BV17-FIX-SCOPE as RESOLVED (via E-13, event seq 302).
limitations_explained: This release is diagnostic only: it identifies the BV-17 unit-scaling mechanism but does not fix BV-17 or any ACTUAL-read mechanism, and could reveal multiple contributing causes rather than one.
The BV-17 fix (SR-FIX-BV17-UNIT-SCALING) cannot be deployed or verified within the contest timeframe because billing-config is a read-only tool surface.

The question of whether correcting BV-17 requires reprocessing/crediting already-issued bills (and the fleet-wide affected v4.2 account count) was tracked as VOB-U-BV17-FIX-SCOPE; state shows this and U-BV17-FIX-SCOPE as RESOLVED (via E-13), but the solution design text still describes it as open/unresolved and blocking dependent scope items — a flagged inconsistency between stated rationale and current evidence/state.
No automated bill writes occurred or are proposed; any correction/credit must go through a logged Billing Operations Human Gate per constraint K-BILLWRITE.

Handoff integrity of H-MDMS-BILL and H-FIELD-BILL remains UNKNOWN (delivery_status and semantic_validity unverified); a silent pipeline defect could still contribute to the unexplained ACTUAL-read dispute segment, and this follow-up was deferred as infeasible in contest time.
Assumption A-MDMS-DATA-RELIABLE (that MDMS export data is reliably delivered and semantically valid) remains an unverified ACTIVE assumption underlying evidence derived from DA-MDMS (E-10, E-12).
Some portion of dispute volume may reflect legitimate billing-error catches rather than noise, so a full return to the pre-August baseline (~600/month) is not guaranteed even after remediation.
The cause of the majority (59%, 1,785 bills) of disputes, which are built on ACTUAL reads, remains unestablished and is deferred as an open unknown (U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE).
